newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Investors eye special Boots payout.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Investors eye special Boots payout.

text.p: Prospects for a special dividend payout will be on the agenda for investors when British healthcare and pharmacy group Boots Co Plc reports annual results next Thursday.

Press speculation that the retailer could be working on a plan to return more cash to shareholders boosted Boots' shares this week. But retail analysts said on Friday it would be surprising to see another display of largesse so soon after Boots' 300 million stg share buy-back last June.

"But there's no smoke without fire," said one analyst who asked not to be identified, adding that a special dividend could be an option for Boots, which has never been shy of stating its willingness to consider handing surplus cash to shareholders.
But the company's cash mountain at the year-end is expected to fall this time to around 250 million stg, reflecting the impact of last year's buy-back.

The retailer, also owner of Halfords car accessory chain and home improvement stores Do It All, is expected to deliver around a seven percent rise in profits before tax and exceptional items. The range of forecasts is between 525 million stg and 540 million, up from 493.5 million a year ago.
Analysts see a dividend of around 20.5 pence a share, up from 18.5 pence.
The core business, Boots The Chemists, is expected to produce around a five percent increase in sales on a comparable store basis.
Analysts want to see if Do It All and home decorating business A.G. Stanley will have perked up as a result of the upturn in home improvement.

Do It All's underlying performance may have improved, but it is expected to see its losses broadly unchanged at around 10 million stg. This is partly because Boots has taken on W.H. Smith Group Plc's share of the chain's losses after buying Smith out last year.

Investors also want an update on when Boots over-the-counter healthcare business Boots Healthcare International will move back into profit. BHI made a loss last year of 8.2 million stg, after investment of 74 million in marketing and developing new products, which include Nurofen pain relief and cold remedy and Strepsils.
"The acid test will be over the next 12 to 18 months when the pay-off should begin to show through," said John Richards at NatWest Markets.
The group is also likely to join the loyalty stakes, and announce the nationwide roll-out of a loyalty scheme it has been testing in the south west and east of England, analysts said.
Boots is experimenting with expansion overseas with pharmacies due to open in the Netherlands and the Far East, which will mean an increase in costs, analysts said.
The shares, which hit a record 740 pence recently, are seen as a safe bet in an increasingly nervous retail sector.
"Boots is a safe and healthy option in an accident prone sector," said Richards at NatWest.
The shares were down 16.5 pence at 708.5 pence by 1535 GMT on Friday, in a weak overall market.
